<action type="say">
Here’s how to do it in Outlook desktop (Windows/Mac are very similar). This assumes you’re the organizer of “Research Sync”:

1) Open the calendar
- In Outlook, click the Calendar icon in the bottom-left.
- In the date picker, go to December 2025, then click Dec 9.

2) Open the “Research Sync” meeting
- In the calendar grid on Dec 9, double‑click the “Research Sync” meeting at 10:30–11:30am.
  - Make sure it says “Meeting” and lists attendees, not just an appointment.

3) Change the date to Dec 10
- In the meeting window, locate the Start time and End time fields near the top.
- Change the date (but not the time) in:
  - Start time: change the date from Dec 9 to Dec 10, keep 10:30 AM.
  - End time: change the date from Dec 9 to Dec 10, keep 11:30 AM.
- Confirm the time zone is still Eastern if it’s visible (usually it is set correctly by default).

4) Send the update to attendees
- Click Send Update (Windows: top-left of the meeting window; Mac: also near the top).
- If Outlook asks whether to send updates to all attendees or only those added/removed, choose:
  - Send updates to all attendees.

5) Verify
- Go back to your calendar and switch to Dec 10.
- Confirm that:
  - “Research Sync” shows on Dec 10, 10:30–11:30am.
  - It no longer appears on Dec 9.
- Your attendees should receive an updated meeting email with the new date.

If you’d prefer, I can also walk you through the drag‑and‑drop method on the calendar view instead of editing the time fields.</action>
